title: Cloning and Large-Scale Production of High-Capacity Adenoviral Vectors Based on the Human Adenovirus Type 5
protocol: Clone a gene of interest including promoter and polyadenylation signal into the shuttle plasmid pHM5.
Digest 20 μg of pHM5-GOI and 10 μg of pAdFTC by I-CeuI for 3 hr at 37 °C in a total volume of 100 µl to linearize plasmids.
Purify linearized plasmids using phenol-chloroform extraction followed by ethanol precipitation.
Add 100 μl of phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol and mix gently by inverting the tube several times.
Centrifuge for 2 min at 15,000 x g.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Add 20 μl of sodium acetate (pH 5, 3 M) and 400 μl of ice cold EtOH (99.8%) and mix vigorously.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 15,000 x g.
Remove the supernatant.
Add 300 µl of 70% EtOH.
Centrifuge at 15,000 x g for 2 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Air-dry the DNA pellet.
Dissolve the pellet in 10-20 µl of dH2O.
Digest I-CeuI-digested pHM5-GOI and pAdFTC plasmid with PI-SceI (10 U) at 37 °C for at least 3 hr or overnight in a total volume of 50 µl.
Purify I-CeuI and PI-SceI digested plasmids using phenol-chloroform extraction followed by EtOH precipitation.
Dissolve DNA in 20 µl of nuclease-free dH2O.
Separate pHM5 plasmid backbone (2.8 kb) and the GOI on a preparative agarose gel.
Gel-purify the GOI using a commercial gel- and PCR-clean-up kit.
Dephosphorylate I-CeuI and PI-SceI-digested pAdFTC with Calf Intestinal Alkaline Phosphatase (10 U) for 1 hr at 37 °C in a total volume of 25 µl.
Purify dephosphorylated plasmid pAdFTC by phenol-chloroform extraction and subsequent EtOH precipitation.
Elute DNA in 20 µl of nuclease-free dH2O.
Perform analytic gel electrophoresis from an aliquot of the dephosphorylated pAdFTC plasmid.
Analyze whether digests are complete and the sizes of the expected fragments are correct (~31 kb for linearized pAdFTC).
Set up the ligation reaction in a total volume of 20 µl using 400 U of T4 DNA ligase and a molar ratio of vector to insert of 1:3.
Ligate at 16 °C overnight.
Perform phenol-chloroform extraction followed by EtOH precipitation.
Elute the DNA in 15 µl of nuclease-free dH2O.
Digest the purified ligation reaction with SwaI (10 U) for 2 hours at 25°C in a total volume of 20 µl.
Concentrate and purify the DNA by performing phenol-chloroform extraction followed by EtOH precipitation.
Elute the DNA in 10 µl of nuclease-free dH2O.
Transform 2 µl of the purified SwaI digested ligation product by electroporation into DH10B or DH5α electrocompetent E. coli.
Select clones for 16 -24 hr at 37 °C on ampicillin-containing LB plates (50 mg/ml ampicillin).
Prepare plasmid DNA mini-preparations using alkaline lysis followed by phenol-chloroform extraction and subsequent EtOH precipitation.
Perform an analytical digest of plasmid mini-preparations followed by agarose gel electrophoresis to check the size of DNA fragments.
Amplify a correct clone in ampicillin-containing LB medium (50 mg/ml ampicillin).
Perform a midi- or maxi-plasmid preparation using any commercially available plasmid purification kit.

Digest 20 µg of the pAdFTC-based adenoviral production plasmid containing the cloned GOI from step 1.11 in a total volume of 100 µl using NotI (20 U) at 75 °C for >2 hr and perform phenol-chloroform extraction twice followed by EtOH precipitation.
Dissolve in 20-30 µl sterile dH2O.
Check an aliquot of 1:10 diluted digested pAdFTC-GOI-DNA by gel electrophoresis.
Culture 116 cells in MEM eagle medium supplemented with 10% FBS and hygromycin B (100 µg/ml).
Seed low passage (below passage 10) 116 cells (~0.4 x 10^6 cells) in a 60-mm tissue culture dish one day before transfection to reach 50-80% confluency the next day.
Transfect linearized HCAdV genome into 116 cells using calcium phosphate transfection or commercially available transfection reagents.
Incubate transfected cells for 16-18 hours.
Remove the medium from the cells and add fresh medium (MEM, 5% FBS).
Infect cells with HV AdNG163R-2 at a ratio of 5 transducing units per cell.
Gently move the dish every 20 minutes during the first hour after infection.
Cultivate infected cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Monitor for cytopathic effects (CPE) caused by virus replication, which is observable 48 hours post-infection.
If CPE occurs earlier than expected, reduce the amount of HV used.
If CPE starts later than expected, increase the amount of helper virus.
Harvest cells and supernatant 48 hours post-infection using culture medium.
Label harvested cells as passage 0 (P0).
Split P0 into two fractions.
From 0.5 ml of detached cells, spin down the cells for 3 minutes at 2,000 x g.
Remove the medium from the cell pellet and store it for isolating genomic DNA (gDNA) for qPCR analysis.
Store cell pellets at -20 °C until further processing.
Freeze detached cells at -80 °C or in liquid nitrogen three to four times.
Thaw frozen cells at RT or in a 37 °C water bath three to four times.
Resuspend thawed cells in their medium and label the lysate as P0.
Mix 1 ml of fresh media (MEM, 5% FBS) with 2.5 ml of P0 lysate to a final volume of 3.5 ml.
Add HV applying 2 TU per cell.
Remove medium from a 60-mm dish of 116 cells and add the viral mixture to the cells.
Repeat steps for obtaining lysates of passages P1 and P2.
Mix 17.5 ml fresh media (MEM, 5% FBS) with 2.5 ml of the P2 lysate and add HV applying 2 TU per cell.
Remove medium from a 150-mm dish of 116 cells and infect cells with the viral mixture.
Cultivate infected cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 48h.
Harvest cells to obtain passage P3.
Freeze and thaw the resuspended cells containing P3 release viral particles 3-4 times.
Isolate gDNA from cell pellets using a commercial DNA isolation kit or another method of choice for each passage during pre-amplification steps (steps 2.6-2.10).
Store isolated gDNA at -20°C if not used immediately.
Generate a standard curve using plasmids containing the GOI in HCAdV genome, ranging from 10^1 to 10^9 copies for qPCR analysis.
Perform qPCR analysis of cell samples from each passage during preamplification steps (steps 2.6-2.10) to determine the number of HCAdV genomes present.
Analyze the same amount of gDNA from P0- P3 using qPCR.
Apply qPCR using 400 nM primers specific for the GOI in the HCAdV genome.
Set qPCR program with pre-incubation at 95 °C for 10 min.
Conduct amplification in 40 cycles of 95 °C for 10 sec, 55-60 °C for 15 sec, and 72 °C for 20 sec.
Add 900 ml of prewarmed MEM supplemented with 10% FBS and hygromycin B into a spinner culture flask.
Remove medium from tissue culture dishes containing 116 cells grown at confluency of 90-100%.
Flush off cells with fresh pre-warmed MEM supplemented with FBS (10%) and hygromycin B using a serological pipette.
Pipette up and down several times to get a homogeneous cell suspension.
Transfer cells directly into the spinner flask containing 900 ml of medium.
Do not use Trypsin/EDTA for suspension cells.
Transfer cells into the spinner flask immediately after removing medium.
Incubate spinner flask on a magnetic stirrer in a tissue culture incubator for 24 hr at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Adjust the magnetic stirrer to 70 rpm.
Monitor cell growth in the spinner culture flask.
Transfer 2 ml from the bioreactor to a 60-mm tissue culture dish prior to adding fresh medium.
Observe cell morphology under a microscope.
Add 500 ml of fresh media (MEM, 10% FBS) supplemented with hygromycin B (100 µg/ml) after 24 hr.
Repeat the addition of 500 ml of fresh media (MEM, 10% FBS) with hygromycin B (100 µg/ml) 24 hr later.
Add 1,000 ml of fresh MEM media (10% FBS) with hygromycin B (100 µg/ml) after 72 hr to reach a total volume of 3 L.
Harvest 116 suspension cells by centrifugation for 10 min at 500 x g at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets in fresh MEM supplemented with 5% FBS by pipetting up and down about 8-10 times to get a homogeneous cell suspension.
Use a total volume of 150 ml for resuspending cells.
Transfer cells from step 4.8) to a 250-ml storage bottle equipped with a sterile magnetic stir bar or a 250-ml small scale spinner flask.
Co-infect cells with the virus within the lysate from P3 (step 2.10.2) and 2 TU of HV per cell.
Assuming a density of 3 x 10^5 cells per ml, add 1.8 x 10^9 TU of the HV.
Stir the cell-virus mixture on a magnetic stirrer in the tissue culture incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 2 hr at 60 rpm.
Transfer the total volume of the cell-virus mixture back into the 3-L spinner culture flask.
Add 1,850 ml of fresh pre-warmed (37 °C) MEM media supplemented with 5% FBS to a total volume of 2 L.
Incubate in the tissue culture incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 48 hr at 70 rpm.
Harvest cells by centrifugation for 10 min at 890 x g at room temperature in 500-ml centrifuge tubes.
Remove the medium and resuspend pelleted cells in a total volume of 28 ml of DPBS.
Pipette up and down to obtain a homogeneous cell suspension.
Freeze the cell-virus suspension in liquid nitrogen or at -80°C, ensuring it is completely frozen.
Store the cell-virus suspension at -80°C until starting the virus purification.
Thaw the viral lysate from step 4.11 in a water bath at 37°C four times.
Centrifuge the viral lysate at 500 x g for 8 min at room temperature and collect the supernatant containing HCAdV.
Weigh 37.5 g of CsCl powder (for 1.5 g/cm³), fill up with dH2O to 25 ml, stir until solution becomes clear, and sterile filter it.
Remove 1 ml of each solution and weigh it on a fine scale to check whether the density is correct; 1 ml should weight 1.5 g.
If necessary, adjust the density by stepwise addition of small volumes (µl) of sterile dH2O and measure the density again until the correct density is achieved for each solution.
Repeat the procedure until density is correct.
If the density is too low, adjust it by adding small amounts of CsCl powder.
Sterile filter it again and check the density.
If the density is still too low, add more CsCl, sterile filter it again, and check the density.
If the density is too high, adjust it by adding dH2O as described before.
Prepare CsCl step gradients in 6 clear ultracentrifuge tubes.
Pipette 0.5 ml of 1.5 g/cm3 CsCl solution into each tube.
Pipette 3 ml of 1.35 g/cm3 CsCl solution on top of the previous layer.
Pipette 3.5 ml of 1.25 g/cm3 CsCl solution on top of the previous layer.
Overlay ~4.5 ml of cleared vector supernatant from step 5.2 on top of the 1.25 g/cm3 CsCl layer.
Centrifuge the gradients in an ultracentrifuge using a swing out rotor (SW-41) at 12 °C for at least 2 hr at 226,000 x g (35,000 rpm) with slow acceleration and deceleration.
Carefully remove layers of cell debris and empty particles.
Collect 1 ml of the lower bands from each tube.
Transfer virus into a sterile 50 ml tube using a clean pipette tip.
Add up to 24 ml of 1.35 g/cm³ CsCl solution to the collected virus particles.
Mix carefully.
Fill centrifuge tubes with 1.35 g/cm³ CsCl-virus solution to the top.
Centrifuge O/N (18-20 h) at 226,000 x g (35,000 rpm) at 12 °C in an ultracentrifuge using a swing out rotor (SW-41).
Collect the HCAdV present in the prominent lower band.
Remove upper layers from the top using a pipette to avoid empty particles.
Take away the lower band containing collected virus using a pipette.
Cut off a strip of dialysis tubing (MWCO: 50,000) of about 8 cm in length.
Wash the dialysis tubing with sterile dH2O for 3x.
Close one side of the dialysis tubing with a plastic clamp.
Transfer the collected virus into tubing using a 1-ml pipette.
Avoid air bubbles within the tubing.
Close the other side of the dialysis tubing with a plastic clamp.
Dialyze in 1-L of dialysis buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 10% glycerol, and 1 mM MgCl2 in deionized H2O) for 2 hours at 4 °C with slow stirring.
Exchange dialysis buffer with 2-L of dialysis buffer.
Dialyze overnight at 4 °C with slow stirring.
Alternatively use a sucrose buffer (140 mM NaCl, 5 mM Na2HPO4x2H2O, 1.5 mM KH2PO4 , and 730 mM sucrose, pH 7.8).
Collect dialyzed virus particles from step using a 1-ml pipette.
Prepare multiple aliquots of desired small volumes (25-100 µl).
Store purified virus at -80 °C.
Dilute 25 µl of the final vector preparation with 475 µl of lysis buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 10 mM EDTA (pH 8.0), 0.5% SDS).
Gently shake for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge for 2 minutes at room temperature at 15,000 x g.
Measure absorbance at 260 nm four times using 100 µl of the supernatant.
Calculate mean value of the four measurements.
Calculate number of viral particles per ml (vp/ml) using the formula: vp/ml = (mean A260) x (20) x (1.1 x 10^12) x (36 kb / HCAdV size in kb).
Seed HEK293 cells in 6- or 12-well tissue culture plates to reach 90% confluency the next day.
Infect cells of one well with 1 µl and a second well with 10 µl of purified virus from step 5.9.3.
Harvest cells 3 hr post infection.
Remove medium from infected wells.
Add trypsin to cover the whole well.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 5 min.
Flush off the cells with trypsin using a pipette.
Spin down the cells at 890 x g for 3 min at RT.
Resuspend the pelleted cells in 200 μl of DPBS.
Wash the cells thoroughly to remove free vector particles.
Centrifuge the mixture for 3 minutes at 890 x g at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cell pellets in 200 µl of fresh DPBS.
Vortex cells resuspended in 200 μl of DPBS for 3 seconds.
Add 200 μl of SDS solution (10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 10 mM EDTA pH 8.0, 0.5% SDS) to the vortexed cells.
Add 20 µl of Proteinase K (20 mg/ml) and vortex again for 3 seconds.
Incubate the mixture at 55 °C for 12-16 hours with slow shaking.
Add 2 μl of RNAse A (20 mg/ml).
Incubate the mixture for an additional 30 minutes at 37 °C.
Add 350 µl of phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol and centrifuge for 2 min at 15,000 x g.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube and repeat this step once.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube, add 50 µl of sodium acetate (pH 5, 3 M) and 1 ml of ice cold EtOH (99.8%) and mix suspension.
Centrifuge samples for 10 min at 15,000 x g to pellet genomic DNA.
Remove the supernatant, add 500 µl of 70% EtOH and centrifuge for 2 min at 15,000 x g.
Remove the supernatant, add 500 µl of 70% EtOH and shake for 30 min at RT.
Centrifuge for 2 min at 15,000 x g.
Remove the supernatant and air-dry DNA pellet.
Resuspend the DNA pellet in 120 µl of dH2O and incubate for ~1 hr at 37 °C while shaking.
If DNA solution appears viscous, shake it for several hours at 37 °C, or incubate at 55 °C for ~1 hr.
Set the PCR program to pre-incubation at 95 °C for 10 min.
Perform amplification in 40 cycles of 95 °C for 10 sec, 55 °C for 10 sec, and 72 °C for 20 sec.
Interpolate the total number of adenoviral genomes using the standard curve.
Calculate the number of adenoviral genomes in the final vector preparation.
Perform qPCR to amplify a part of the adenoviral late gene 3 (L3) present in the HV genome.
Use a plasmid carrying the adenoviral late gene 3 (L3) to generate a standard curve.
Apply 400 nM of L3 forward primer and 400 nM of L3 reverse primer.
Add 300 nM of the L3-specific probe.
Set the PCR program to pre-incubation/activation at 95 °C for 10 min.
Run amplification during 40 cycles of 95 °C for 15 sec and 60 °C for 1 min.
Use a universal probe PCR mastermix for the qPCR reaction.
Calculate the number of infectious HV particles in the final vector preparation using the standard curve.
Calculate the ratio of absolute infectious HCAdV particles to HV contamination levels to evaluate the quality of the vector preparation.
